findings.claim: `Accept-Query` is added only to the `RequestHeader` type union; if the module has a parallel runtime list (e.g. an exported `const requestHeaders = [...] as const`, a validation Set, or a matching `ResponseHeader` union), those will now be out of sync with the type.
findings.rationale: Only this one hunk is shown, so I cannot verify whether a runtime array or a sibling union exists in the same file. Hand-maintained header lists in TS very often have both a type union and a runtime `as const` array (or a separate ResponseHeader union), and adding to one without the other silently breaks lookups/validation at runtime while type-checking passes. Worth confirming the rest of headers.ts. Low-to-moderate confidence since the file content outside the hunk is unknown.

findings.claim: `Accept-Query` (RFC 9727) is defined as a *response* header advertising the query formats a resource accepts for the QUERY method, not a request header, so listing it under `RequestHeader` may be semantically wrong.
findings.rationale: Per RFC 9727, `Accept-Query` is sent by the server in a response (typically to OPTIONS) to indicate supported QUERY content types. The surrounding union does already mix in response-only names such as `Accept-Patch`, `Accept-Post`, `Accept-Ranges`, and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`, so this file may intentionally be a combined list — in which case this is a non-issue. Flagging so the author can confirm the union's intended semantics; moderate confidence about the RFC, low confidence that it matters here.
